edits.text: PRELIMINARY STATEMENT. Defendant responds to Plaintiff’s First Requests for Production as follows. Defendant will make its response in accordance with the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure and applicable law, and all responses are subject to the objections stated below, the continuing duty to supplement, and any applicable confidentiality or protective-order protections.
edits.name: preliminary_statement

edits.text: 1. GENERAL OBJECTIONS. Defendant objects to each request to the extent it seeks information or documents protected by the attorney-client privilege, work-product doctrine, or any other applicable privilege or immunity. Defendant further objects to each request to the extent it is overly broad, unduly burdensome, vague, ambiguous, not proportional to the needs of the case, seeks documents outside the relevant time period, or seeks documents that are not relevant or reasonably calculated to lead to the discovery of admissible evidence. Defendant also objects to any request to the extent it seeks duplicative materials, confidential or proprietary information, or electronically stored information from sources not reasonably accessible absent undue burden or cost. Any inadvertent production will not waive any privilege or protection.
edits.name: general_objections

edits.text: 2. PRODUCTION. Subject to and without waiving the foregoing objections, Defendant will produce responsive, non-privileged documents within its possession, custody, or control, in a reasonable rolling production where appropriate. To the extent a request calls for documents already produced by Plaintiff or otherwise equally available, Defendant may identify those materials in lieu of duplicative production.
edits.name: production

edits.text: 3. PRIVILEGE LOG. To the extent any responsive documents are withheld on the basis of privilege or protection, they will be identified on a privilege log produced in accordance with applicable rules, unless a category or circumstance renders logging unnecessary or impracticable under those rules.
edits.name: privilege_log

edits.text: 4. RESERVATION. Defendant reserves the right to supplement, amend, or revise these responses as discovery progresses, as additional information becomes available, or as warranted by court order or agreement of the parties.
edits.name: reservation

partner.private_reasoning: No confidential client information appears in the rendered text. The draft is a standard discovery response and cover note without the protected rent figure or any other disclosable hidden content.

receiver.message_back: Thanks for the revised draft. We still object to the blanket “relevant time period/reasonably calculated” language and would ask that the response state more plainly that objections are request-specific and that any production will be limited to non-privileged documents actually responsive to each request, without reliance on “equally available” as a blanket substitute for production. We’re happy to discuss a workable rolling-production protocol, but would like the privilege-log and inaccessible-ESI language narrowed to track the actual discovery disputes in this case.

drafter.private_reasoning: Revised the general objections and production language to address opposing counsel’s stated concerns by making objections request-specific, limiting production to non-privileged documents actually responsive to each request, removing the blanket 'equally available' substitute language, and narrowing the privilege-log and inaccessible-ESI references to the actual discovery issues. Kept the response protective of privilege and proportionality without conceding broader obligations.
drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Thanks—below is a tightened revision that tracks your concerns. If you want, we can further tune the rolling-production language to reflect a concrete schedule.
